data.narrative:
Cognition is a Series C artificial intelligence and software company founded by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan that has raised $1.5B+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR) within the AI & Software sector, including stage-matched companies Figure AI ($39.0B), Skild AI ($14.0B), and Crusoe Energy ($10.0B).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised ($1.0B) as a proxy baseline and applying a typical Series C step-up multiplier of 1.7x, implies a valuation of $1.7B. Peer-median analysis across the three same-stage, same-sector comparables yields a median valuation of $14.0B, with a range spanning $10.0B to $39.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneity in AI company revenue traction and market positioning at this stage.

Triangulation of both methods produces a low estimate of $1.4B, a median of $7.8B, and a high of $16.1B. The spread between stage-progression and peer-median results—a roughly 8x range—reflects material uncertainty around whether Cognition's product adoption and go-to-market execution track closer to earlier-stage capital-deployment patterns or to the more mature traction of Figure AI. Key uncertainties center on unit economics, customer concentration, and the sustainability of AI software monetization at scale.
